label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L>=7), sequence-content dependent
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (t == L, recall_idx 0). It never fires during the original or copy phases. Within delimiter steps the firing rate goes up steeply with sequence length: 0 for L<=4, 0.1% at L=5, 1.2% at L=6, 3.1% at L=7, 4.7% at L=8, 5.7% at L=9 (as a share of steps). L=8-9 hold about 73% of the activation mass. Only about 23% of L>=7 delimiter steps fire, so whether it fires depends on what the sequence contains. It is enriched when the first token (the token about to be output) is b, g, m, h, 0, 3, z or p: adding that condition gives F1 0.47 on dev, but recall drops to 0.47. It is also enriched when the prefix has many of x, m, v, 1, l, n. Neither of these explains it cleanly, which suggests a distributed readout of the hidden state. Magnitude is largest for L=9 sequences with those first tokens.
